modules.module_title: Collect trip information and plan for meals for the trek/expedition

pcs.pc_description: collate all the required information from the tour operator/expedition/trip leader such as the itinerary of the trek/expedition, altitude gain, distance to be covered and the difficulty level of the program.
check and note the budget allocated with the trip leader/ organizer for provision shopping and load cartage and plan all procurement and meals accordingly.
record names of all the group members with food allergies or any other dietary restrictions if any.

create meal plans, menus and recipes, keeping in mind the nutrition, special dietary requirements and previous reports/client feedbacks from similar trips, with the expedition/trip leader/tour operator considering the assigned budget

make a detailed list of provisions including special/alternative food items to be procured to cater to group members and guests with allergies and/or special dietary requirements, and kitchen equipment to be carried, keeping in mind the number of days without road support or access.
plan the roles and work distribution for the kitchen helpers.
supervise the kitchen helpers to clean and check the burner, fuel line and functioning of each stove before packing it to ensure they are in good working condition.
hand over the list of items to be procured to the kitchen helpers or procurement incharge.
oversee that the necessary items for the trip, including provisions, fuel and LPG cylinder for the stove have been procured and arrive on time.
plan re suply and stops to procure fresh vegetables, fruits, eggs, non veg and dairy items so as to make them last efficiently without spoilage.
find solutions to procurement issues in the event of unavailability of provisions.
ensure the purchased materials are composed of healthy ingredients and the expiry date is at least one month post projected completion of the trip.
double check the items purchased and ensure the materials are adequate for the duration of the camp and the number of people on the expedition/trek.
plan on the number of loads for kitchen supplies and provisions and tally that against the porter / pony numbers.
maintain an account of all the expenses incurred with supporting bills to be submitted to the trip leader or as defined by company SOP.

modules.module_title: Pack equipment and supplies needed for the expedition

pcs.pc_description: guide the kitchen helpers to pack the provisions and appropriate number of equipment, such as stoves and cylinders, kitchen repair kit and light weight utensils for cooking and eating.
ensure a balance is maintained while packing and the supplies to be carried is neither excess nor too less in quantity.
ensure that fuel/cylinder required for the stove is packed in leak proof fuel bottles or gas cylinder, which ever may be applicable.

modules.module_title: Set up the kitchen and dining tent and prepare meals

pcs.pc_description: coordinate with the kitchen team to set up and arrange the kitchen tent before the group arrives
ensure that toilet tents are nowhere close to kitchen or dining facilities.
appoint duties to the kitchen helpers and instruct and supervise them while they perform the same.
operate backcountry stoves.
prepare well balanced, nutritional food keeping in mind allergies and other dietary restrictions of guests and colleagues.
ensure to taste the cooked food before serving.
organise meals as per the meal plans.
ensure that the kitchen team is awake early in the morning to keep packed lunch and breakfast ready.
ensure warm washing water and tea/coffee is available at wake up call time.
ensure that kitchen staff is well groomed and shaved at all times.
supervise the kitchen staff to keep the kitchen clean and presentable, at all times, for client inspection.
ensure proper action and immediate course correction in case of any allergic reactions or food poisoning cases in the camp.
follow segregation protocol in case of any cases of diarrhea or other contagious cases in camp.
improvise on the spot in case of missing provisions.
offer help to persons with disabilities when asked for.
empathize with and respect persons with disabilities.
adhere to “Minimum Impact '' travel policies and not throw/burn any non biodegradable items like plastic wrappers, cigarette buds, bottles and tins.
ensure to use biodegradable packing material, wherever possible.

ensure that all kitchen related activities such as kitchen tent set up, washing hands and vegetables and cleaning utensils post lunch are carried out at least 200 ft. away (Or as far as the camping site allows) from all water sources. (Rivers, streams, fresh water springs, waterfalls, high altitude lakes).
ensure not to dig pits to bury any dry or wet waste such as paper, plastics and tins in the mountains or in the camp.
ensure not to feed waste food to any wildlife.
avoid excessive food wastage
ensure to carry back left over food, or leave it in shallow pits covered with earth, if not possible to do so
ensure not to cause damage to the fragile habitats and environments (animal life, flora and fauna) found in the wilderness.

kus: KU1. feedback and reporting formalities as per company SOPs.
KU2. waste disposal norms and techniques.
KU3. equipment and provision packing techniques.
gs: GS1. provide feedback to the team.

modules.module_title: Follow ethical environmental practices while packing up a campsite

pcs.pc_description: ensure that all used plastic, tin cans and paper items are packed so that they can be brought back from the trek/expedition for proper disposal.
direct the kitchen team to dispose off vegetable peels and other wet food waste as per environmental guidelines/company SOPs.
oversee that all waste for disposal to be taken to the city/town is segregated and adequately packed

modules.module_title: Pack and return all kitchen equipment and submit trip report

pcs.pc_description: ensure that the kitchen tent is cleaned, all equipment is packed and returned to the organizer.
check for any damage to the tent or stove and report it to the organiser.
ensure all unused ration is returned to the organizer.
provide feedback about the kitchen helpers to the organiser.
record and inform about any incidents / accidents within the kitchen team to the organiser.
provide feedback to the organizer on the meal plans, including client feedback, and suggest changes (if any) for future expeditions.
provide feedback on the quality and quantity of the equipment used during the expedition such as back country stoves, LPG/fuel etc.
report any additional expenses incurred during the expedition.

modules.module_title: Ensure to Take Safety Measures While Cooking

pcs.pc_description: identify hazards associated with using backcountry MSR and LPG stoves.
oversee that all safety precautions are taken by the kitchen team to avoid accidents like burns and cuts.
ensure food, fuel and chemicals are always kept away from each other in order to avoid contamination.
keep a record of all food allergies (if any) and dietary restrictions and prepare meals accordingly.
instruct the kitchen helpers on a daily basis to ensure that special meals made for people with allergies and dietary restrictions are always kept separate from the rest of the food.
follow instructions from the trekking guide/ trip/expedition leader during an emergency.
ensure everyone wears proper footwear in the kitchen as stoves are always at ground level and prone to spillages.
check expiry details on every food item and throw away expired food.
choose the kitchen tent site carefully to safeguard from avalanche, rockfall, treefall, flooding and lightning.
establish communication with the expedition leader/ trip leader/ mountaineering instructor in case of a natural disaster.
improvise menu during a natural disaster to ensure supplies are used judiciously
deal with all eventualities in a calm and composed manner.
